about.title: Agoura Hills Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Agoura Hills sits along the US-101 corridor in Los Angeles County, home to office parks, retail centers, and light-industrial businesses tucked between the hills. Workers here face the same on-the-job risks as anywhere: falls, equipment accidents, repetitive strain, and vehicle collisions while making deliveries along Agoura Road or Reyes Adobe Road. In most cases, California law channels workplace injuries through the workers' compensation system rather than a lawsuit against the employer. But when someone outside the employment relationship contributed to the injury, a subcontractor, a property owner, a defective tool manufacturer, or another driver, a separate injury claim may be possible alongside a comp claim. We handle workplace injury cases and can review the details of what happened to explain which paths may apply to you. There's no obligation to move forward, and no fee unless we recover something for you.

items.title: Understanding Which Claim Applies
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against an employer, but a negligent third party can open the door to a separate claim. We can help sort out which routes are available to you.

items.title: Knowing the Reporting Window
items.desc: California generally requires an injured worker to report a workplace injury to their employer within 30 days. Missing that window can complicate a claim, so understanding the timeline matters early on.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: Employers aren't allowed to punish or retaliate against a worker for reporting an injury or filing a claim. We can help you understand your rights if you're worried about how reporting might be received.

items.question: I was hurt while making a delivery near US-101 in Agoura Hills. Is this a workers' comp claim or something else?
items.answer: It could be both. If another driver caused the collision while you were performing work duties, you may have a workers' comp claim against your employer's insurance and a separate third-party claim against the at-fault driver. We can review the details of the crash and your job duties to sort out which claims apply.

items.question: Can I get in trouble with my employer for reporting a workplace injury?
items.answer: No. California law prohibits retaliation against employees who report injuries or file workers' compensation claims. If you're concerned about how your employer might react, we can explain your protections and options before you report.

items.question: How long do I have to report an injury or file a claim after getting hurt at work in Agoura Hills?
items.answer: Generally, you should report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days. If a third party outside your employer contributed to the injury, a separate claim against them typically carries a two-year deadline. Because these timelines can overlap and get confusing, it helps to talk with us sooner rather than later.
